Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:1:1.hebrew: מגורשת ואינה מגורשת בעלה חייב במזונותיה - וכגון שייחד לה ארעא אחריתי, דאי לאו הכי אין לו חזקה; דכיון דאית לה מזוני, מזוני הוא דקא אכלה, כדאמרי' לקמן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:1:1.english: "Divorced yet not divorced — her husband is obligated in her sustenance" - And [this is] where, for example, he designated for her another field; for if not so, he has no chazakah [of ownership in the field she is using]. For since she is entitled to sustenance, it is [merely] her sustenance that she is eating [from it], as we say below.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:2:1.hebrew: ראייתן ראיה ומעמידין שדה בידן - נראה לרשב"א דנקט תרוייהו איידי דבעי למיתני גבי גזלן: "אין ראייתו ראיה ואין מעמידין שדה בידו". דהתם איצטריך תרוייהו, דאי לא תנא אלא "אין ראייתו ראייה", הוה אמינא דאין ראייתו ראיה לגבי הא שאין מעמידין שדה בידו, אבל מעות יש לו; דלא ה"א טעמא אי לאו דאודי ליה הוה ממטי ליה ולחמריה לשחוור, אלא הוה מפרשינן טעמא משום דתליוהו וזבין לא הוו זביניה זביני, אפי' מנה לו מעות. הלכך קאמרי תרוייהו דאין ראייתו ראיה כלל, דאפי' מעות אין לו, דטעמא הוא משום דאי לאו דאודי ליה כו'. והאי "כולן" נראה לרשב"א דקאי נמי אבן שלא חלק ואשה שלא נתגרשה. ואע"ג דאמר לקמן [גבי אשה בנכסי בעלה] דלגלויי זוזי הוא דבעי, כיון דאוקימנא בהודאה לא שייך בה גלויי זוזי; ועוד, דמשמע לקמן דסבירא להו לרב הונא ולרב נחמן דלא אמר לגלויי זוזי הוא דבעי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:2:1.english: "Their proof is a proof, and we establish the field in their possession" - It appears to the Rashba that [the Gemara] stated both [clauses] because it wants to teach, regarding a robber: "His proof is not a proof, and we do not establish the field in his possession." For there, both are necessary: because if it taught only "his proof is not a proof," I would have said that his proof is not a proof with regard to [the matter] that we do not establish the field in his possession, but he does have [a claim for his] money. For I would not have said that the reason is [that] had he not admitted to him, he would have brought him and his donkey to Shachvor; rather, we would have explained the reason as being because "if they hung him and he sold, his sale is not a valid sale," even if [the buyer] counted out money for him. Therefore they state both, [to teach] that his proof is no proof at all, for he does not even have [a claim for] money, since the reason is that had he not admitted to him, etc. And this "all of them" appears to the Rashba to refer also to a stone that was not divided and a woman who was not divorced. And although [the Gemara] says later [regarding a wife, in her husband's property] that he [only] wants to reveal [that he has] money, since we established it as [a case of] admission, revealing money is not relevant to it; and moreover, it is implied later that Rav Huna and Rav Nachman hold that he did not say that he wants to reveal money.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:2:2.hebrew: ומעמידין שדה בידן - גבי אומן נמי שייך שדה, כגון אם הוא בנאי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:2:2.english: "And they establish a field in their possession" - With regard to an artisan too, a field is relevant, for example if he is a builder.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:4:1.hebrew: אבל בשטר קנה - אלקח מן האיש וחזר ולקח מן האשה נמי קאי, כדמוכח במתני' בהניזקין (גיטין דף נח: ושם). וקשה, דתניא בסוף מי שהיה נשוי (כתובות דף צה. ושם ד"ה וכתבה): כתב לראשון ולא חתמה לו, לשני וחתמה לו — איבדה כתובתה. דוקא משום דלא חתמה לראשון, אבל אי חתמה לראשון לא איבדה כתובתה, כדמוכח התם, אע"פ שכתבה שטר. ונראה לר"י דהא דקאמר רב "בשטר קנה", יש להעמיד בשטר הראיה שאחר הקנין, דכיון שאחר הקנין עשתה שטר שייפתה כחו כל כך, קנה. וההיא דכתובות מיירי בשטר מתנה בלא קנין אחר אלא שטר. א"נ "חתמה" דהתם לשון גמר, כמו "חתמו" גבי תורף דגיטין, וכמו "תורה חתומה ניתנה" בהניזקין (גיטין דף ס.), כלומר שגמרה מקח ונתרצתה בעל פה. אי נמי חתמה ממש, ובשטר של בעל. והא דאמר רב "בשטר קנה" — שעשתה שטר מכירה בשמה. ומסתבר דטעמא דרב כטעמא דשמואל, דאמר בהניזקין (שם דף נח. ושם ד"ה אבל): אף בשטר לא קנה עד שתכתוב לו אחריות. ושמואל לטעמיה, דאמר בפ"ק דב"מ (דף יד. ושם): אחריות לאו טעות סופר בשטרי מקח וממכר; ורב סבר: אחריות טעות סופר הוא. אבל קצת קשה, דלקמן פריך לרב הונא דאמר "תליוהו וזבין זביניה זביני" מהא דאמר שמואל "אף בשטר לא קנה", ואי תלוי הדבר באחריות, מאי קשה ליה משמואל טפי מרב:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:4:1.english: "But with a document, she has acquired" - This applies to [the case where she] bought from the man and then bought again from the woman as well, as is proven in the Mishnah in [the chapter] Hanizakin (Gittin 58b, there). But this is difficult, for it was taught at the end of [the chapter] Mi Shehayah Nasui (Ketubot 95a, there, s.v. "vekhatvah"): If she wrote [a document] for the first one but did not sign it for him, and [then] for the second one and she did sign it for him — she forfeits her marriage contract. [This is] specifically because she did not sign for the first; but if she had signed for the first, she would not forfeit her marriage contract, as is proven there, even though she had written a document. And it appears to R. Yitzchak that when Rav says "with a document, she has acquired," this should be established as referring to a document of proof [written] after the act of acquisition; since after the acquisition she made a document, which strengthened his claim so much, he has acquired. And that [passage] in Ketubot speaks of a deed of gift without any other act of acquisition besides the document. Alternatively, [the word] "she signed" there is an expression of finalizing, like "they signed" regarding the essence of a get in Gittin, and like "the Torah was given sealed" in [the chapter] Hanizakin (Gittin 60a), meaning that she finalized the sale and agreed orally. Or else she actually signed, [but] in a document of the husband. And [as for] what Rav said, "with a document, she has acquired" — [this means] that she made a bill of sale in her own name. And it is reasonable that Rav's reasoning is like Shmuel's reasoning, who said in [the chapter] Hanizakin (ibid. 58b, there, s.v. "aval"): Even with a document, he does not acquire until she writes for him a guarantee. And Shmuel is consistent with his view, for he said in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (14a, there): A guarantee clause is not a scribal error in documents of sale and purchase; whereas Rav holds that a guarantee clause is a scribal error. But it is somewhat difficult, for later [the Gemara] challenges Rav Huna, who said, "If they hung him [by force] and he sold, his sale is a [valid] sale," from this [statement] that Shmuel said, "even with a document he does not acquire"; and if the matter depends on the guarantee, what difficulty does [the Gemara] have from Shmuel any more than from Rav?

Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:6:1.hebrew: ורב ביבי מסיים בה כו' - ק"ק הלשון, דהא רב ביבי פליג כדאמרי' לקמן, ורב הונא לא מיירי בהכי אלא בהודה ולא במנה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 47b:6:1.english: "And Rav Bibi concludes it, etc." - The wording is somewhat difficult (kashe katzat), for Rav Bibi disagrees, as we say later, and Rav Huna is not speaking of this, but of [a case where the debtor] admitted [the debt] and not [a case of] a maneh.
